product: Commercial-stage multi-product company: Attruby (acoramidis), a near-complete TTR stabilizer for ATTR-CM approved in US, EU, Japan, Switzerland, Brazil, and UK; BBP-418 (ribitol) for LGMD2I/R9; encaleret for ADH1; oral infigratinib for achondroplasia; plus hypochondroplasia, chronic hypoparathyroidism, and an ATTR depleter.
demand: Strong. Attruby growth is led by treatment-naive first-line starts with rising first-line share and stable net patients added; US achondroplasia treatment penetration is only about 25% versus 60-75% in Europe, which management frames as expandable demand rather than share-only.
pricing_power: Moderate. BridgeBio says it will not chase Pfizer's discounts, claims the lowest-priced ATTR-CM product with the best 30-month data, and aims for parity access; but Pfizer rebating slowed share gains, and the Aug 31 2026 US government agreement expands Medicaid access while the company says it avoids future pricing mandates.
competition: Crowded in ATTR-CM: Pfizer Vyndamax, Alnylam Amvuttra, Ionis Wainua, plus tafamidis generics near 2031. Achondroplasia has BioMarin VOXZOGO and Ascendis Yuviwel injectable CNP products. Management says BBP-418 has no competition in LGMD2I/R9.
team: CEO and co-founder Neil Kumar; Chief Commercial Officer Matt Outten; Chief Business Officer Chinmay Shukla; Julie Everett COO Skeletal Dysplasias; Ananth Sridhar CEO BridgeBio Endocrinology. A September 2026 wire listing referenced adding Dr Peter Lebowitz to the Board and a senior finance/BD hire; that release was not read in full.
market_strategy: Hub-and-spoke decentralized model with autonomous disease teams and a central clinical, regulatory, and commercial hub. Strategy is clinical differentiation plus parity access for Attruby, pre-launch diagnosis and awareness building via dedicated ICD-10 codes and MDA care centers, funding three simultaneous launches with about 1.7B USD pro forma cash.
bull: Q2 2026 revenue $243.7M with $222.4M Attruby US net product revenue, volume-led first-line starts; three NDAs filed, BBP-418 PDUFA 2026-11-27, encaleret 2027-05-08, ~$1.7B pro forma cash.
bear: Attruby share gains slowed by Pfizer rebates and shrinking second-line pool; ~$100M quarterly operating losses, $879M deferred royalties, KKR sold 5M shares 2026-08-14; consensus target 109.1 is perverse per §17.
falsifier: BBP-418 receives a CRL on or before its 2026-11-27 PDUFA date, or Attruby sequential US net product revenue fails to grow from $222.4M in Q3 2026.
web_what_changed: Q2 2026 results Aug 10 2026: total revenue 243.7M USD including 222.4M USD US Attruby net product revenue, growth led by treatment-naive starts. All three NDAs now submitted: encaleret accepted Jul 22 2026 (PDUFA May 8 2027), BBP-418 PDUFA Nov 27 2026. 1B USD preferred equity closed Jul 1; KKR sold 5M shares Aug 14; US government access and pricing agreement Aug 31.
web_not_known_yesterday: No company event dated Sep 24 or Sep 25 2026 was found on the IR news page or recent 8-K list. Newest items are Sep 23 2026 acoramidis real-world benefit versus tafamidis reducing risk of clinical worsening, and Sep 18 2026 inducement grants under Nasdaq Rule 5635(c)(4).
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume-led. Growth comes from first-line treatment-naive starts and rising Attruby share rather than price; management expects roughly 25M-30M USD sequential quarterly sales growth and holds premium price while Pfizer rebates. Mix is shifting to first-line as the second-line switch pool normalizes.
web_suppliers: not found. No API, manufacturing, or supplier disclosures appeared in the Q2 2026 earnings release, the reviewed 8-K exhibits, or the Morgan Stanley conference transcript, so no evidence of supplier constraints was located.
web_customers: Payers and PBMs, specialty pharmacies, hospital systems, and concentrated rare-disease prescribers: about 150 MDA Care Center sites for LGMD2I/R9 achondroplasia, over 2200 identified ADH1 patients at roughly 70 new diagnoses monthly. UnitedHealthcare rebate pressure is cited; no customer revenue concentration was disclosed.
web_who_loses: Pfizer loses first-line ATTR-CM share and pricing leverage with Vyndamax tafamidis. Alnylam Amvuttra and Ionis Wainua lose second-line silencer volume. BioMarin VOXZOGO and Ascendis Yuviwel face an oral alternative in achondroplasia if oral infigratinib is approved.
web_contradicting_evidence: Shares near 66 USD versus 109.1 USD consensus target with negative 63-day momentum (-3.4%) and only 8 visible analyst actions versus 11 firms cited by the engine. Second-line switch market is shrinking and Alnylam cut 2026 TTR guidance. Pfizer discounts and a UnitedHealthcare rebate exist. Break-even guided only late 2027 or early 2028, with 879M USD deferred royalty obligations. KKR sold 5M shares Aug 14. Tafamidis generics arrive around 2031.
web_if_management_right: Attruby reaches 4B USD peak sales with 30-40% peak share and blockbuster 2026; BBP-418, encaleret, and infigratinib launch across 2026-2027 toward about 10B USD pipeline peak sales; operating break-even late 2027 or early 2028 then cash generation; infigratinib US launch mid-2027 and EU early 2027.
web_if_management_wrong: Attruby US net price and share stall first if Pfizer rebates cap access and second-line keeps shrinking, breaking revenue already annualized near blockbuster level. Then cash: about 100M USD quarterly operating losses, 879M USD deferred royalty obligations, 1B USD preferred equity. A BBP-418 or encaleret CRL compounds it.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Bayer, which markets acoramidis ex-US as BEYONTTRA and pays royalties starting near 30% and tiering up; CDMOs and specialty pharmacies supporting three launches; TTR diagnostics and cardiac imaging; MDA care network sites; genetic testing labs diagnosing LGMD2I/R9 and ADH1.
